set.body:
Wire the neural semantic channel (embed-onnx MiniLM) into the Sherlock recall-to-video runner.

Why: the diagnostic baseline uses lexicalJaccard for both nomination and the cost model. Recall
language and coder language share few stems, so a large share of unit mass lands in
external(attributed) that a semantic encoder should recover. BenchChannels.neural already turns an
OnnxSentenceEmbedder into a SemanticDistance with a stated NeuralEncoder identity; the runner just
never asks for it.

Slice:
- Runner reads STORYMODEL4S_ONNX_MODEL / STORYMODEL4S_ONNX_TOKENIZER; when both are set it opens
  the pinned AllMiniLmL6V2 encoder (checksum-verified at open) and builds the channel over the
  segmented recall units (query role) and the annotation node texts (document role): leaf text is
  the row description, scene text is the scene label. When unset, the lexical baseline runs and the
  summary says so - the channel kind is printed, never inferred.
- The same SemanticDistance feeds CandidateGenerator (perLevel=8) and DefaultLocalCostModel, so
  nomination and scoring see one geometry.
- Artifacts live in gitignored tmp/onnx/, fetched from the pinned HF revision
  1110a243fdf4706b3f48f1d95db1a4f5529b4d41; sha256 verified against the catalog pins
  (model 6fd5d72f..., tokenizer be50c362...) before first use, and again by the embedder at open.

Evidence to produce: scoped gate on embed-bench (JVM), plus a before/after comparison of external
mass and anchored-unit counts across the 33 recall transcripts, lexical vs neural, same inputs.
set.title: Neural semantic channel (embed-onnx MiniLM) in the Sherlock recall runner
